speech: Implement a Java 17 student-directory library. Add a student and update an existing student. Support fast case-insensitive exact full-name lookup and first-name prefix lookup. There may be tens of thousands of students; performance matters.
question: Implement a student directory
text: TL;DR: Use stable IDs, full-name buckets and an ordered first-name index. This initial reference assumes single-threaded access.

facts.text: Add students and update existing students.
Fast case-insensitive exact full-name lookup and first-name prefix lookup for tens of thousands of students.
Single-threaded access is an initial assumption, not a stated guarantee.

speech: When I said remove, that was a correction: I mean update. Deletion is not required.
question: Clarify required operations
text: TL;DR: Keep add and update; no public deletion operation is needed. Internal removal of old index entries is part of an update.

facts.text: Add and update are required; deletion is not required.

speech: The library can be used concurrently; consider updates and lookups at the same time.
question: Concurrent access
reason: The initial unsynchronized reference cannot update several indexes atomically.
text: TL;DR: Protect all directory operations with one shared lock. The previous unsynchronized implementation needs revision.

facts.text: Concurrent reads and writes must preserve cross-index consistency.

speech: Could an atomic counter generate student IDs?
question: ID generation and thread safety
text: TL;DR: One library monitor now protects IDs and every index operation. AtomicLong is optional for IDs; by itself it would not protect the indexes.

facts.text: An atomic counter was suggested for IDs, not mandated as the entire concurrency design.

speech: Your name-to-student map is wrong; several students can have the same first and last name. Add the same name ten times and there must be ten records with different IDs. Look at the highlighted map in your code.
question: Duplicate names
text: TL;DR: Names are lookup keys, not identity. IH's reference already stores sets of IDs per name, so ten equal names remain ten records; the feedback concerns unseen candidate code.

facts.text: Equal first and last names still represent distinct students with unique IDs.
Feedback about a highlighted map describes unseen candidate code, not IH's reference.

speech: When an existing student is renamed, every affected index must be updated consistently. Keep the same student ID.
question: Rename invariants
text: TL;DR: Update removes the old index memberships and adds the replacement under the same monitor, retaining the ID. Readers cannot see a half-updated directory.

facts.text: Renaming retains the student ID and updates every affected index consistently.

speech: That finishes the student-directory problem. Now an independent question: application latency is intermittent while CPU and memory appear normal. How would you investigate?
question: Diagnose intermittent application latency
text: TL;DR: Separate queueing, dependency latency, locks and pauses using traces and timings. Low CPU does not rule out blocked threads.

speech: How would repeated thread dumps help distinguish waiting from deadlock?
question: Thread-dump diagnosis
text: TL;DR: Compare several dumps to identify persistent waits, lock owners and cycles. A single waiting stack is not proof of deadlock.
